title: TLS path: no graceful drain on shutdown
description: main.rs:108-149 — The TLS accept loops are spawned with tokio::spawn and main() simply awaits shutdown_signal() then returns. When main() exits, the tokio runtime drops all spawned tasks, including in-flight HTTP connections being served in the nested tokio::spawn at line 138. These connections are cancelled mid-request with no drain. The plain HTTP fallback path uses axum::serve with_graceful_shutdown which properly drains in-flight connections; the TLS path has no equivalent. This can cause data loss for requests in flight at shutdown time (e.g., a Message/set being written when SIGTERM arrives).
